chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' from Aban from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorces his wife while she is pregnant, [asking]: Does he marry her sister before she gives birth? He said: He does not marry her until the waiting period is complete. The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as: If it is a revocable divorce in which he has the right of return, based on the reports we have previously presented, and they included that if he divorces her with a final divorce, it is permissible for him to contract marriage with her sister even if she has not exited the waiting period. Those reports are detailed, and acting upon them is more preferable than acting upon this general report.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his wife's sister while his first wife is in her divorce waiting period?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction by distinguishing between revocable (raj'i) and final (ba'in) divorces, prioritizing specific reports over this general one. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'takhassus' (specification), where detailed evidence overrides general statements in legal derivation. It underscores the precision required in applying iddah rules to polygamous unions within the same family.
